Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Old Doc Khonshu Versus New Croc Ammit", "body": "Chance built the episode title around a reading of Khonshu's beaked bird skull as a plague doctor mask, the herb-filled remedy of an older age. In his view Khonshu stands for the old medical model of remedy after injury, while Ammit, who judges before any harm is done, stands for prescription in advance. Harrow, Khonshu's former avatar, becomes the old doc turned new croc, and the hosts point to his lines about the cure being a little taste of the disease, and medicine and poison differing only by dosage, as what they call predictive programming for preemptive medicine."}, {"title": "Mirrors, Two Pillars and Initiation", "body": "The hosts track initiation symbolism scene by scene: a security guard named JB, which they hear as the temple pillars Jachin and Boaz, the checkerboard shirt Steven wears all episode, the matching lamps framing the HR office where he is fired, and the pyramid paperweight a police officer picks up and questions. The mirrored storage unit is read as a psychomantium, the mirror box once used to commune with spirits, and the broken mirror that traps Steven as a sign that his alter now lives in the mirror world. Even the mirrored pyramid at the fight is compared to a Masonic tracing board."}, {"title": "Hidden Meanings in Names and Languages", "body": "Gabe reads the actor's name as a stack of archetypes: Isaac, the sacrifice reversed on the mountain, and a scarab hiding inside Oscar. Spector is tied to the Brocken spectre, where a shadow could be cast over the people below, and Marc spelled with a c to brandy and alcoholic spirits. Layla is said to mean night, pairing her with the moon. Chance calls Harrow's remark that his followers each learn three languages direct disclosure of a priestly cult working through Greek, Hebrew and Latin puns at once, what he calls a phonetic kabbalah."}, {"title": "Name Tags, Passports and the Straw Man", "body": "When Steven is fired and hands in his name tag, Chance links it to the ren, the Egyptian name that forms a layer of the spiritual body and is renewed at initiation. Steven's public persona is read as the straw man he surrenders just before collecting Marc Spector's passport from a storage locker, where the clerk knows his face better than he does. The hosts dwell on the passport asking for lawful aid rather than legal process, and Gabe finds a Rosicrucian 93 and the year 87 in the prop passport's numbers, plus a USA that he says points to Esau."}, {"title": "Jacob, Esau and the Stolen Birthright", "body": "Gabe hears the Jacob and Esau story running under the whole episode. Harrow shares a bowl of lentils with Steven, echoing the porridge Esau traded for his birthright, and minutes later Harrow takes the scarab from an old man in an alley, holding his hands the way Jacob dressed in skins to take his father's inheritance. The scarab, inscribed with a Book of the Dead prayer to Khepri, becomes the heirloom Steven loses when he throws off his coat to fight, while the hosts note how Layla keeps turning up wherever the scarab goes."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Your dynamic Disney-Marvel decoders are back at it again to take another Moon Knight. Exploring the second episode, we'll reveal themes relating to the morphing of medical freedom into technocratic dictatorship, the hidden cult of the dark goddess, sky clock symbolism and the liminal space between languages.
